scope_warning: This matrix is computed against the C4C commission tree. That tree does NOT contain the accepted D01/D02/G01 successor contracts. See scope_defect below. Every conclusion must be re-derived on the combined C1+C3 execution tree before it can support O1-C05.

scope_defect.finding: THE C4C TREE IS NOT THE C4 EXECUTION TREE
scope_defect.detail: Omega-1 O1-C01 already established that the C1 commission/result head is not an execution-ready C1+C3 tree. This lane independently confirms it at the code-identity level and adds that the three runtime-sensitive successor contracts themselves are absent.
scope_defect.consequence_for_this_lane: The D01 declared-encoding lane and the D02 opaque naive date/time carrier — the two most runtime-sensitive C4 operations — have NO contract in the tree this lane was asked to qualify. Runtime qualification against a pre-repair decoder cannot discharge O1-C05 for the governed C4 run.
scope_defect.not_asserted: This lane does not assert WHERE those contracts live or whether they are correct. That is C4A's lane. This lane records only that they are absent from the tree under qualification.

findings: The int-to-float64 conversion is performed INSIDE the pyreadstat C extension (READSTAT_TYPE_DOUBLE -> np.float64). SavNumericReader and int2code are NOT identifiers in this repository; the C-level step has no repository-side implementation to test.

type(native_code) is not int at pre553_r5_codec.py:177 is an EXACT TYPE IDENTITY check. np.int64 fails it; bool fails it. The caller must supply a genuine Python int, whose provenance is the numpy-scalar .item() unwrap at pre553_physical_decoder.py:168-172 plus caller-side int(...). Any change to the scalar boxing type closes G01.

reader_version is part of the SHA-256 physical-metadata digest (pre553_physical_decoder.py:500-508 -> :229 -> :247-261). Therefore ANY pyreadstat version change invalidates every frozen physical-metadata digest, including all retained C3 and retained Route-B receipts. This is the widest blast radius of any runtime fact in the repository.

The pyreadstat 1.3.2-equivalent-to-1.3.6 claim is DOCUMENTARY ONLY — asserted from upstream ReadStat C source blob hashes (readstat_value.c and readstat_sav.c blob-identical; readstat_sav_read.c differing only in the multiple-response-set parser context). No probe in this repository re-proves it.
P03 observed: np.float64 is an isinstance(x, float) subclass, so _jsonable RETURNS IT UNCHANGED rather than unwrapping it; NaN maps to None.
operations.runtime_class: PURE_PYTHON_DETERMINISTIC for the bit-token layer; LIBRARY_VERSION_COUPLING for the arrival-typing layer
operations.non_mac_qualification_implication: Two separable claims. The float64 BIT token layer is host-independent and already probe-proved on this surface (P01, all nine authorised tokens matched 3ff0000000000000-style big-endian forms, roundtrip OK). The ARRIVAL TYPING layer (whether the reader yields a Python int, an np.int64, or a Categorical) is unproved on any non-Darwin build and additionally depends on the UNPINNED formats_as_category default (P14: True).

operations.name: D02 built-in naive date/time carrier behaviour
code_sites: rawlsing_next/pre553_r5_codec.py:122-127 (isinstance guard rejecting date/time/time/datetime with R5CodecError)
rawlsing_next/pre553_physical_decoder.py:159-177 (_jsonable: datetime has NO .item(), so it falls to :177 return str(value))
rawlsing_next/gt34_obl031_q69b_comparator_resolver_r2.py:92 and rawlsing_next/v3_adp010_oee_executor.py:162-172 (tz-awareness checks; bare fromisoformat Z-handling — OFF the C4 source path)
findings: IN THIS TREE THE D02 CONTRACT DOES NOT EXIST. There is no opaque date/time carrier. pre553_r5_codec.py:126 rejects date/time, but that guard is UNREACHABLE from the decoder route because pre553_physical_decoder.py:177 already collapsed the value to str().

P03 measured the exact D02 collapse on this surface: datetime.date(2008,4,5) -> '2008-04-05'; datetime.datetime(2008,4,5,6,7,8) -> '2008-04-05 06:07:08' (SPACE separator, not ISO 'T'); datetime.datetime(..., tzinfo=utc) -> '2008-04-05 06:07:08+00:00' — a DIFFERENT STRING, therefore a DIFFERENT semantic_hash, from the naive form; np.datetime64('2008-04-05','D') -> '2008-04-05' versus np.datetime64('2008-04-05T06:07:08','s') -> '2008-04-05 06:07:08'. So the NUMPY DATETIME64 UNIT SELECTION changes the D02 rendering, and the numpy version is not pinned by any gate.

P14: the two reader options that actually govern the date carrier — dates_as_pandas_datetime (default False) and disable_datetime_conversion (default False) — are NOT passed anywhere in the repository. Whether a SAV date variable arrives as datetime.date, datetime.datetime, or a pandas datetime64 column therefore follows the installed pyreadstat build's defaults, not any frozen contract.

Omega-1 O1-C04 explicitly forbids inferring datetime.date versus datetime.datetime from the historical rendered value 1582-10-13 and requires recording the actual current subclass. On a non-Mac surface the actual subclass is UNOBSERVED, so O1-C04 cannot be discharged there without a probe.
rawlsing_next/pre553_source_backed_c11_facade.py:127 couples value-label lookup to str(raw) — the same rendering that D02 is meant to replace.
explicit_not_found: TYPED_DATE identifier — NOT FOUND anywhere in the repository, any file type
operations.non_mac_qualification_implication: This is the operation that most directly cannot be inherited by name. The Omega-1 requirement is to record the ACTUAL current subclass on the actual execution surface. On a candidate non-Mac surface that subclass has never been observed, and the two governing reader defaults are unpinned. A source-free probe of date/datetime arrival typing on the candidate build is mandatory before the physical claim.

findings: read_file_in_chunks IS DEPENDENT ON THE KWARG NAME chunksize. P06 measured the installed signature: (read_function, file_path, chunksize=100000, offset=0, limit=0, multiprocess=False, num_processes=4, num_rows=None, kwargs). The repo passes chunksize=, encoding=, apply_value_formats=, user_missing=; the latter three travel through **kwargs.
apply_value_formats=False IS correct and required (else value labels become cell text), and is passed.

Stata extended-missing token normalisation at pre553_physical_decoder.py:286-289 handles BOTH the bare 'a' and the dotted '.a' shape. That dual-shape handling exists precisely because the token pyreadstat returns for Stata extended missing has differed across versions. The reader_token/stata_token strings ENTER the physical-metadata digest, so a build emitting 'a' where a frozen receipt expects '.a' silently changes the digest.

classify_physical_value at pre553_physical_decoder.py:296 uses isinstance(value, float) — true for np.float64, so NaN collapses to SYSTEM_MISSING. But a pandas nullable pd.NA would match NO branch and fall through to OBSERVED_STORAGE_VALUE at :305, silently changing a missing-state classification.

The banked LiTS AS2B builder imports duckdb, numpy, pandas, pyarrow and pyreadstat at MODULE SCOPE and is exec_module'd onto the live path. P12 measured duckdb ABSENT on the available surface. So pandas, pyarrow AND duckdb must all be importable on the LiTS path, and pandas/duckdb are absent here.

fiabc_lits_i_representation_authority.py:40-48 RECORDS reader_version and python as part of its authority identity, so changing either changes REPRESENTATION_AUTHORITY_HASH — but nothing in the DTA lane ENFORCES the installed version. Contrast the WVS7 lane, which does enforce it (see OP-06).
operations.non_mac_qualification_implication: The DTA reader option surface is the same unpinned-default surface as OP-01/OP-03, plus the extended-missing token shape, which is an explicitly acknowledged pyreadstat-version fork. A non-Mac surface requires a source-free probe of the extended-missing token shape and of NaN/NA collapse before the physical claim.

operations.name: Resource measurement accounting (peak RSS)

measured_result.note: ru_maxrss is BYTES on Darwin and KIBIBYTES on Linux. A value recorded on one OS is not comparable to the other and must never be relabelled across an OS boundary.

operations.non_mac_qualification_implication: Any C4 measurement budget expressed in ru_maxrss is NOT portable to a non-Mac surface. O1-C07 requires frozen expected budgets and retained measured counts; those budgets would have to be re-derived per surface, and the retained R8B Darwin unit law cannot be inherited by name.

additional_runtime_sensitivities_found.finding: pandas is an UNPINNED TRANSITIVE dependency of the governed read path. No production module imports pandas, yet the decoder calls DataFrame.itertuples(index=False, name=None) and does positional zip(variables, row) binding. Whether a cell arrives as int, np.int64, float, np.float64, str, np.datetime64 or pandas NA is decided by pandas dtype inference. The retained anchor records pandas 2.3.3 (C3 receipt) and 2.3.1 (accepted checkpoint) — conflicting — and the available surface has NO pandas at all.

reader_version enters the physical-metadata SHA-256 digest. Widest blast radius: a pyreadstat version change invalidates every frozen physical-metadata digest in the repository, including accepted C3 holdings and retained Route-B receipts.

struct.pack(">d") and explicit int.from_bytes(..., "little"/"big") make the float64 bit-token layer and the SAV header-layout layer HOST-ENDIANNESS INDEPENDENT. Confirmed by P01 (all nine authorised tokens matched and round-tripped). Also rawlsing_next/pre553_empirical_objects.py:181-221 semantic_hash is pure Python, forbids float, applies no unicodedata, and uses sort_keys with explicit separators.

Decimal.normalize() rounds to the PROCESS-GLOBAL decimal context precision (P08 measured default prec=28). No repository code mutates getcontext().prec, so this is stable today, but it is a process-global coupling rather than an explicit one.

These hashes depend on the Unicode Character Database bundled with CPython. P10 measured unicodedata.unidata_version 14.0.0 on this surface (CPython 3.11.3). UCD differs across CPython minor versions. These modules are in the R6/GT34 layers, NOT on the current C4 semantic-hash path; flagged so HQ does not let them enter a C4-authority scope unproved.

Bare datetime.fromisoformat accepts a trailing 'Z' only from CPython 3.11+. P09 measured that 3.11.3 accepts '2008-04-05T06:07:08Z' and the repo carries an explicit Z->+00:00 workaround at v3_adp010_oee_executor.py:172 that documents the 3.10/3.11 boundary. Off the C4 source path.

There is NO dependency lock of any kind in the repository (P13/01_AVAILABLE_ENVIRONMENT.json lock_search). Six tracked CI workflows install pytest and pandas UNPINNED on ubuntu-latest with python-version "3.11" (major.minor only). No workflow carries pytest==9.1.1 or pandas==2.3.3. O1-C05 requires a frozen dependency inventory; it CANNOT be derived from this repository and must be AUTHORED.

Install-on-import is ABSENT from rawlsing_next/, tests/ and .rabochii/. The previously-recorded C3-02 defect (import-time pip install pandas in the D02 semantic test) is not present in this tree. No `pip install --upgrade` or `--target` occurs in tracked Python. The archived install-on-import occurrences live only in content-addressed archival objects under data/ddm_build_copy/recovery_reservoir/ which no production module imports. O1-C05's no-install-on-import and no-silent-upgrade clauses are satisfied by the current tree.

The governed bounded court enforces env {PYTHONHASHSEED: 0, PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD: 1}, which removes third-party pytest-plugin nondeterminism. But rabochii_execution_protocol.py:342-344 validates python_version only at the 3.N major.minor grain, so the patch level floats, and NO repository assertion anywhere pins the pytest version.

The python.org framework 3.11.3 primary launcher is a ZERO-BYTE file and exits 0 emitting nothing; only the python3.11-intel64 alternate (70544 bytes) runs. This independently defeats the assumption that the anchor interpreter is simply present and usable on this host. It is a reported environment defect, not a qualification fact, and it is recorded so HQ does not treat 'CPython 3.11.3 is on PATH' as satisfied by observation.

That packet records disposition FAIL_SOURCE_FREE_QUALIFICATION with result "48 passed; 10 fixture setup errors; 0 failed tests; exit code 1" on CPython 3.12.14 / pytest 9.1.1, with failure_summary naming an at07 fixture content-hash mismatch. This is the closest existing precedent for interpreter substitution and it is a FAILURE. No repository code establishes whether that failure was interpreter-induced or fixture-induced, and this lane does NOT reinterpret it either way. It is cited as a reason to require an explicit pre-run qualification rather than to assert that 3.12 cannot work.
